comment: The site demo video's storyboard: positions and durations, never titles. Compiled by tools/site_video.py (`compile_storyboard`) to the dump driver's key schedule. Virtual time only advances on clean frames, so a duration is a duration of the FILM, and `gates` fails any beat whose picture was still visibly moving 0.2 s before the next beat's key (`gate_beats_at_rest`, on decoded frames). The film is shot with the hold hint taught (`plxnative-hintoff`, armed by `site_video.py render --storyboard`, recorded as `hold_hint: suppressed` in render.json): the capsule is a one-time teaching overlay and a film has no viewer to teach, so a rest on a card is as long as it reads calm. Up from the hero lands on the Home pill (a page's Up lands on its own pill) and the profile chip is one `left` from it, so the harness signs the simulator in to the mock's Demo account and the chip reads Demo, never Sign in, should a beat press `left` there. The hero pages: `right` on the Info button turns the carousel forward and `left` on the Continue button turns it back (the app's own edge rule), so the film turns to the second page and back to the first before it goes down to the shelf. OK on the shelf's third card opens that title's Detail (the default Continue Watching press opens details; the no-playback gate proves nothing played). `down` there scrolls the page to its Cast & Crew row, where the catalog's `people` gives every performer of that title a portrait, and four more `down`s run through the rest of the page to its foot: the title's collection (its linked heading, then its shelf), More Like This, and the About section, where the film rests. Arrows only: nothing on the page is opened (a portrait's or a card's OK is another page, the About card's a reader), so a miscounted press changes where the page rests and nothing else, and `back` leaves the Detail from wherever it is scrolled. Keys that belong to one gesture share a beat, pressed `gap_ms` apart without waiting for rest: the rest gate judges a beat's END, and a remote pressed faster than the springs settle is what the film is there to show. The Movies page (the Library redesign: one header row over the full poster grid, no shelves) is walked with arrows only, never OK, so no count of presses can open a title, a collection or a menu there: the page opens on the header row, `down` into the poster grid, `right` `right` `down` `right` inside it (never the letter rail's column), then four `up`s walk back out of the grid to the header row (the Library's `back` takes one region a press: header, tab bar, Home), and one `back` returns to the bar and Home, where `down` lands on Continue. A `back` pressed lower down jumps the page to its top first, and that jump is NOT filmed: the first Linux render of it wrote different frames under the hold-injection gate (104 frames), so it is not yet a motion the dump can vouch for. Loop: the last frame is the first frame's composition (Home, hero, focus on Continue); `end.match_first_frame` is read by `gates` (`storyboard/loop`): the last frame may differ from the first by at most 1/255 in a channel.
